dedupe_keys.name: environment agency historic landfill sites england

description: Historic Landfill Sites maps every known landfill in England that no longer has an environmental permit in force, including sites that pre-date landfill regulation and sites whose licences were surrendered or revoked. Each polygon has up to 34 attributes describing where the site was, when it was used, who operated it and what was deposited, with licence dates, first and last waste input dates and waste types where records exist. The producer is the Environment Agency, drawing on its own records and those of local authorities; much of the pre-licensing information comes from a national survey in the early 1990s. Coverage is England at site level, digitised at 1:10,000 and updated every six months. Data download free as GeoPackage, GeoJSON, shapefile or geodatabase from the Defra data services platform, under the Environment Agency Conditional Licence with attribution to the Agency and local authorities. Caveats: records are incomplete where information was lost, the Agency is not the regulator of these sites, surrendered sites may move from the authorised landfill layer later than they appear here, and boundaries are approximate. Simulation uses: exposure of closed landfills to coastal erosion, sea level rise and river flooding (waste release risk), and siting constraints for new infrastructure. Related records: Ontario Landfills (data-ontario-landfills) covers an equivalent inventory in Canada.
